insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (varies as per Policy Schedule; examples mention 5L, 7.5L, 10L, 15L, 20L, 25L, 50L, 1Cr, Unlimited)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: (i) Room Rent (Any Room), Boarding, Nursing Expenses as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home
great.reference: Section II - Coverage > BASIC COVER > 1. In-patient Treatment (page 5/37)
great.explanation: Room rent is covered for “Any Room” along with boarding and nursing expenses as provided by the hospital/nursing home. This avoids room-rent caps and the claim reductions that usually come with them.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
great.quote: Pre-hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 90 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalized.
great.explanation: Medical expenses are covered up to 90 days immediately before hospitalization. This gives a longer window than the usual 30–60 days for tests, consultations, and medicines leading up to admission.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured... Sum Insured will be restored unlimited number of times and maximum up to 100% each time... 2nd Claim (For Same / different illness)
great.explanation: Sum insured is automatically restored an unlimited number of times, up to 100% each time, for the 2nd claim for same or different illness. This can significantly increase usable cover in a year if there are multiple hospitalizations.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: Cumulative Bonus... 50% of sum insured for each claim free year and maximum up to 100%... Cumulative bonus will not be reduced unless the same is utilized in the event of claim... unutilized Cumulative bonus will be carried forward
great.explanation: Cumulative Bonus increases by 50% of sum insured for each claim-free year up to 100%, and it is not reduced unless it is utilized in a claim. This helps your bonus stay intact even after a claim if the bonus portion wasn’t used.

great.name: Organ Donor Expenses
great.quote: Organ Donor Expenses... Note: The coverage limit under this benefit is upto the sum insured and over and above the sum insured.
great.explanation: Organ donor expenses are covered, and the note states the limit is “upto the sum insured and over and above the sum insured.” This indicates donor costs may not eat into your base sum insured, improving protection for transplant scenarios.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatments: The following procedures will be covered... g) Robotic surgeries ... h) Stereotactic radio surgeries ...
good.explanation: Modern treatments including robotic surgeries and stereotactic radio surgeries are covered. Since no specific “no sub-limit” wording is shown in the quote, it is safest to treat this as covered but subject to policy terms/limits up to sum insured.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 30-day waiting period – Code Excl 03 (Not Applicable for Accidents)... within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness claims are not covered in the first 30 days from policy start, except accidents which are covered immediately. This is standard in retail health insurance and mainly affects early non-accident claims.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception with the insurer. This is within the common 2–4 year market range and is important if you already have known conditions.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Specified disease / procedure waiting period... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are excluded until you complete 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a standard waiting period and can delay coverage for listed conditions even if they are not pre-existing.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post Hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 180 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital.
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered up to 180 days immediately after discharge. This is at the higher end of standard post-hospitalization coverage and helps with follow-up treatment costs.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: Air Ambulance... reimbursement of expenses incurred towards the cost of air ambulance service up to Rs.5,00,000/- in a policy year
good.explanation: Air ambulance expenses are reimbursed up to ₹5,00,000 per policy year. This can be valuable for emergency transfers, but costs beyond this limit will be out of pocket.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: Domiciliary Hospitalization: Coverage for medical treatment (including AYUSH) for a period exceeding three days... taken whilst confined at home...
good.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization is covered for treatment (including AYUSH) exceeding three days when you are confined at home. This helps when hospitalization is medically needed but home treatment is required due to specific circumstances.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Coverage for Non-medical Items (Consumables): Items as per List I will become payable If there is an admissible claim... If insured opts this coverage
bad.explanation: Consumables/non-medical items are payable only if you opt for this optional cover. If you don’t buy the add-on, these items can become significant out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-Payment: Co-payment means a cost sharing requirement... provides that the policyholder / insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
bad.reference: Definitions (page 2/37); Optional Covers include Smart Network co-pay and Voluntary Co-payment (pages 12/37, 16/37)
bad.explanation: Optional covers include co-pay options (e.g., Smart Network co-pay and Voluntary Co-payment), which means you may have to bear a percentage of each admissible claim if chosen. Any co-pay increases your out-of-pocket share on every claim where it applies.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless facility... payments... are directly made to the network provider by the insurer
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available at network providers where the insurer pays the hospital directly. The document excerpt does not specify the number or breadth of network hospitals, so ease of finding a nearby cashless hospital cannot be judged here.
